summary:
The hitting category is the story of the week across every rating, and today's board gives it a perfect target. R4 hitting is scorching at 38-19 (67%, n=57) against a 51% season baseline — a 15.2pt spike — while R3 hitting rides a 5-game win streak at 58% (14d) and R1 hitting checks in at 61% with its own 4-game streak. Trends is the model's most consistent engine, hitting identical 37-20 (65%) marks across all four ratings over the last 14 days with a 3-game win streak each, and it pairs best with sp (57.9%, n=620) and runs (57.1%, n=688) as the top category combos all season. The one category to fade is bullpen_fatigue, cold across the board at 39% (14d) versus a 46% baseline — a repeat -7.8 to -6.4pt drag for every rating, so any play leaning on that signal alone needs extra scrutiny today.

All four ratings are in lockstep on today's slate, with SDP @ MIL the headline consensus: R3 shows the strongest conviction at +2.41 for MIL, and MIL as a liked team has been excellent historically (41-22, 65%, n=63; strong plays 25-12, +15.0u). That's the kind of spot where a hot trends/hitting combo and a proven team-when-liked profile stack in the same direction. ATL @ LAD is the second-strongest consensus, with R3 again leading at +1.00 for LAD — and LAD when liked is the best team on the board by win rate (71%, n=51; strong 27-6, +27.0u), making this the safer, if smaller-delta, play. CHW @ CLE is the only game where all four ratings agree on the road dog (CHW, deltas -0.48 to -0.64), a legit contrarian signal worth respecting rather than fading. NYY @ TBR rounds out the slate with modest deltas (R1-R4 clustered +0.24 to +0.50) favoring TBR, who is 69% (41-18, n=59) and 72% in strong plays when picked — note Gerrit Cole and the Yankees have been a weak liked-team crew all year (51%, -4.0u in strong plays), reinforcing the fade-NYY lean here. Strong-play unit trends remain firmly positive across all four ratings over 14 days (R4 leading at 19-8, +16.0u), so today's board sits in a hot window for the model overall.
